acceptance.criterion_verbatim: hyperlinks clickable, verified against TO-C's measured renderer -- not against the documentation.
acceptance.invocation: TO-C's measurement (tools.py:617/:658 hardcode contentType 'text'; census 8 hits / 71 files) -- no post was made and no Graph call was issued
acceptance.output_evidence:
CANNOT BE SATISFIED UNDER D-PROSE, AND THE CRITERION'S OWN WORDING IS WHY. It says verify against TO-C's MEASURED RENDERER rather than against the documentation -- and what TO-C measured is that the send path posts contentType 'text', under which the content is NOT parsed as markup. So a markup hyperlink is not clickable on the current renderer, and no formatting change can make it so: it needs contentType 'html', which is D-HTML, a gateway code change riding safe-ec2-deploy. WHAT THIS TO DOES INSTEAD, and it is a lesser thing stated as one: a SENTENCE-ENDING url is placed ALONE ON ITS LINE, which is the best available form under 'text'. THAT IS NOT A CLICKABILITY CLAIM. Whether the Teams client auto-linkifies a bare url is UNMEASURED -- observable only by posting, which TO-C was explicitly told not to do and did not. --- D-HTML BUILD APPENDED 2026-08-21T093828Z. BUILD ONLY: nothing applied, nothing posted, nothing above this line changed. --- BUILT: app/teams_format.py now carries format_for_teams_html() beside format_for_teams(), and _blocks() was EXTRACTED so the two renderers cannot drift into two standards -- the only thing that differs between them is how a block is spelled on the wire. HTML emits exactly two tags (

and ), escapes with html.escape(quote=True), and wraps EVERY url in an anchor whose href and anchor TEXT are identical (a link whose visible text differs from its target is the shape of a phishing message; the gateway must never author one, so it is asserted rather than assumed). Battery 14 -> 35 tests, rc=0 captured on the tool; commit-gate rc=0 with 0 WARN lines; 0 non-ascii bytes and 0 CRLF in both files. THE ORDER THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: segment the RAW text on urls, THEN escape each segment -- NOT escape-then-linkify. Escaping first turns ?a=1&b=2 into ?a=1&b=2, and the url pattern (\S+) then swallows a NEIGHBOURING entity's characters: 'see "https://x/a"' escapes to '..."https://x/a"', and a trailing-punctuation strip run over that peels the ';' off " and emits a mangled entity that renders as visible garbage. Segmenting removes the hazard instead of guarding it. A DEFECT INVISIBLE UNDER `text` AND CONSEQUENTIAL UNDER `html`: a sentence-final url arrives with the period attached, and under html that period lands INSIDE the href and breaks the link -- it breaks the exact clickability this change exists to deliver. Split off as trailing text; a BALANCED closing paren is KEPT, because stripping it from a _(disambiguation)-style url produces a confidently-wrong href. MY OWN INSTRUMENT FAILED FIRST, AND IT FAILED TOWARD A FALSE ALARM. The test-side renderer deleted tags outright, so '

Claim it here:

https://...

' fused into the single token 'here:https://...' and the conservation law reported content loss. The OUTPUT was correct -- Teams renders

as a block, and the estate's own inbound stripper (app/tools.py:692) already substitutes ' ' for a tag. THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, NOT THE RENDERER. Rather than trust that fact, it is now asserted at its source (D9 AST test: a tag must strip to a SPACE, never to nothing), because the fusion is LATENT -- it becomes real for every agent reading Teams through this gateway the day that substitution becomes "", and nothing else in the estate would say so. WHY THE STATUS DOES NOT MOVE: the criterion asks for clickability verified against TO-C's MEASURED renderer. The build makes correct anchor markup EXIST; it cannot make a renderer render it. That needs (a) the wiring flip APPLIED and (b) one posted message read by a human. Neither has happened, neither is authorized, and a build cannot discharge a criterion whose subject is a renderer. THE WIRING IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS TREE -- 4 lines, recorded here, unapplied: app/tools.py:617 - message = teams_format.format_for_teams(message) + message = teams_format.format_for_teams_html(message) app/tools.py:618 - payload = {"body": {"contentType": "text", "content": message}} + payload = {"body": {"contentType": "html", "content": message}} app/tools.py:658/:659 -- the identical pair inside send_channel_message THE TWO HALVES MOVE TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL: flipping contentType WITHOUT swapping the renderer collapses every message back into the single wall of text Andrew complained about, SILENTLY, because a blank line is whitespace in HTML. Asserted (D9 test_the_two_halves_must_move_TOGETHER) so the pair cannot land by halves. THE DEPLOY COST, READ AT SOURCE (infra/aws/ec2/opal-gateway/deploy-to-ec2.sh @HEAD) -- the gate's stated condition for this build: MECHANISM: local tarball -> S3 -> SSM -> on-box pull, venv pip install, then `systemctl restart opal-gateway.service`. The service stays UP through the pip step; the outage window is restart -> uvicorn port bind. IT IS A SERVICE RESTART, NOT AN INSTANCE BOUNCE. The script issues no stop-instances / start-instances / reboot and touches the box only over SSM, so THE PUBLIC IP DOES NOT MOVE and the mcp.opalinvest.dev / ALB path is unchanged. (I had priced this leg earlier from a ~100s outage with the public IP moving; that figure describes an instance BOUNCE and does not describe a deploy. Corrected here, once.) THE WINDOW: GATEWAY_WORKERS=1, so there is no second worker to absorb in-flight calls -- every MCP call in flight at the restart is dropped, for every seat, because this is the box every seat reaches MCP through. The script bounds the wait at 30s for `systemctl is-active` and a SEPARATE 30s for `/health`; that second loop exists because of a measured deploy failure on 2026-08-20 (W6-PORT, twice, deterministic) -- systemd 'active' precedes uvicorn's port BIND by several seconds and a single unretried curl "lands in that gap EVERY time on this boot profile". THE PART THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS FROM THE WORD "DEPLOY": every run REWRITES /opt/opal-gateway/.env from Secrets Manager -- Graph creds, the Fernet key, the JWT PEM, both OTP bearers, MS_INGEST_BEARER, and the MASTER_ADMIN / WRITE_CAPABLE roster + ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS. A deploy performed for a FORMATTING change re-derives the gateway's identity and tier configuration, and silently resets any on-box drift. THE QUEUE, MEASURED NOT RECALLED: 3 commits / 3 files under app/ are ahead of EC2_MANIFEST's deployed_commit 5a1cc39e8e -- cdedf37b8f (D-PROSE), 2b7258f31c (alwaysLoad marks, which also touches integrations/opal_portal/integration.py), 90d526c199 (lastModifiedDateTime on the two readers). All three are this seat's and all three are build-only. A D-HTML deploy CARRIES ALL OF THEM, including one change outside the Teams surface entirely -- so the apply is requested as carrying the queue, never as "one formatting change". PLANE, STATED: that queue is measured against the MANIFEST'S RECORD. deployed_commit is a self-report written by the deploy script, and Rule 22a does not let a record stand as applied truth. The act that closes it is an on-box read (SSM md5sum of app/tools.py against the tree), and it belongs to the apply, not to this build. NAMED LATER RUN, SHARPENED: the wiring flip + a gateway deploy on SITE Z (Rule 26 @95b7eeb458 -- the apply runs on the device that owns the work), on Andrew's separate word, followed by ONE posted message read by a human. Only that last step can move D-3.

NON-BLOCKING, RECORDED RATHER THAN BROADCAST (per the 2026-08-21 Andrew-direct surprise-channel directive): A KEY LINE EMBEDDED MID-LINE IS INVISIBLE TO THE STANDARD. _is_key_line() runs over lines from splitlines(), so 'Claim it here:' becomes its own block only when the CALLER already put it on its own line. In a single-line message with no sentence terminator before it ('...reference: TCK-... Claim it here: https://...') it stays inside the prose block and only the url is hoisted. This is D-PROSE behaviour and NOT a D-HTML regression -- both renderers share _blocks(). NOT FIXED, deliberately: splitting on a ':'-terminated clause would also shred 'reference: TCK-...' and every ordinary prose colon, which is a worse failure than the one it repairs, and the caller controls the input. Recorded so the next reader of the standard does not conclude that key lines are detected everywhere.
